title: Align two toy modalities with linear encoders
goal:
CLIP trains two encoders so that matching pairs end up close in a shared space. Here the encoders are linear: `I_f = Xi @ Wi` and `T_f = Xt @ Wt`, the same pattern as the learned projections `W_i` and `W_t` in Figure 3. The loss is the one from Exercise 1, with the features normalized and the logits scaled by `exp(t)`.

Write `loss_and_grads(Xi, Xt, Wi, Wt, t)`. `Xi` has shape `(n, d_i)`, `Xt` has shape `(n, d_t)`, `Wi` has shape `(d_i, d_e)`, and `Wt` has shape `(d_t, d_e)`. Row `k` of `Xi` is paired with row `k` of `Xt`. Return `(loss, dWi, dWt, dt)`: the symmetric loss and its exact gradients with respect to `Wi`, `Wt`, and `t`. The paper's code has no backward pass, because an autodiff framework supplies it, so this exercise derives it by hand.

The tests check your gradients against finite differences and then train a pair of linear encoders with your gradients on two views of the same hidden vectors.
hints: Forward: `If = Xi @ Wi`, `Ie = If / norm`, the same for text, `L = np.exp(t) * Ie @ Te.T`.

The loss is the mean of two cross entropies with the diagonal as the target. Its gradient with respect to the logits is `G = (P_rows + P_cols - 2 * np.eye(n)) / (2 * n)`, where `P_rows` is the softmax of `L` along axis 1 and `P_cols` is the softmax along axis 0.
Since `L = scale * Ie @ Te.T`, the gradients with respect to the normalized embeddings are `dIe = scale * G @ Te` and `dTe = scale * G.T @ Ie`. Note the transpose in the second one.
Normalization has a Jacobian. If `e = f / |f|`, then `df = (de - e * (e . de)) / |f|` for each row: remove the part of `de` that points along `e`, then divide by the original length.
`L` is proportional to `exp(t)`, so `dt = np.sum(G * L)`. Then `dWi = Xi.T @ dIf` and `dWt = Xt.T @ dTf`.
